description.value: This cross-sectional study used fMRI to compare obese and lean adolescents' neural responses to high-calorie, low-calorie, and nonfood images and to examine associations with fasting leptin levels.

value: We hypothesized that obese compared with lean adolescents would display exaggerated responses in neural circuits that encompass sensory and somatic integration-interoception (cortical), emotion-memory (limbic), and motivation-reward (striatal) processes during exposure to HCF and LCF relative to NF pictures.
We further hypothesized that obesity-related alterations in endogenous leptin, insulin levels, and insulin sensitivity would be associated with brain responses to HCF images.

description.value: Participants viewed high-calorie food, low-calorie food, and nonfood pictures and rated liking and wanting.
Participants viewed 42 high-calorie food pictures, such as ice cream and pizza, each presented for 6 seconds, then rated how much they liked and wanted the item on a 9-point Likert scale.
Participants viewed 42 low-calorie food pictures, such as salads and fruits, each presented for 6 seconds, then rated how much they liked and wanted the item on a 9-point Likert scale.
Participants viewed 42 nonfood pictures, such as books and bicycles, each presented for 6 seconds, then rated how much they liked and wanted the item on a 9-point Likert scale.
